newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Volatile zinc prompts metal market turmoil.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Volatile zinc prompts metal market turmoil.

text.p: Wide fluctuations in the price of zinc on Wednesday resulted in chaotic trading in many of the London Metal Exchange's contracts, leaving investors bemused.
"You could not bet on the direction of any of these metals....at least not in the short term," one LME floor trader said.
The zinc market appeared to have absorbed the brunt of the recent selling by late Tuesday and the price began to climb again in early Wednesday business.

This was accompanied by strengthening nearby premiums which convinced traders that Chinese smelters had not yet bought back all their short positions, and that a supply squeeze could still be on the cards.
But in mid-afternoon another large sell order knocked any remaining confidence out of the market and the price plunged from a day's high of $1,520 down to $1,440.
The fall was accompanied by a report that persistently high zinc prices could eventually prompt substitution in some of the metals main markets.
"There is concern because this is a very price-sensitive market," said Jim Birch, secretary of the Zinc Alloys Die-casting Association.
"If we get 12 months of higher prices, it could well have a long term-damaging effect," said Malcom Widows, managing-director of UK die-caster Brock Metal Co.
Copper, aluminium and nickel had been advancing steadily earlier in the day but zinc's fresh fall soon undermined their stability and all swiftly reacted lower.
"Stocks of copper in LME warehouses keep on rising and it may be difficult for prices to mount a sustained rise, at least during the summer," one trader said.
"But aluminium and nickel are showing some tightness and could bounce again," he added.
Copper dropped $77 a tonne to $2,285 before rallying slightly, aluminium from $1,717 to $1,675, and nickel from $7,580 to $7,350.
Other commodity markets were left in the shade by the volatile industrial metals, and generally showed relatively small movements.
